metadata_hints.n_items_test: 1,172 (Challenge test); Challenge dev 299; Challenge train 1,119 (Challenge total 2,590). Companion Easy set: 2,251/570/2,376 (5,197)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_system: DGEM (AI2 decomposed graph entailment model, with ARC Corpus retrieval)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Challenge test; supervised baselines; random guess-all = 25.02; authors state no baseline is significantly above random (95% CI +/-2.5%). Others: TableILP 26.97, BiDAF 26.54, DGEM-OpenIE 26.41, DecompAttn 24.34, TupleInference 23.83, IR (ARC Corpus) 20.26
metadata_hints.lineage: Released together with ARC-Easy and the ARC Corpus (2018-03); later ARC-DA direct-answer variant (AI2, 2021). Unrelated to Chollet's ARC-AGI
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Scores are highly sensitive to evaluation format (scoring options separately vs. showing all options together); Borchmann 2024 argues the 'Challenge' difficulty is largely an artifact of the separate-option setup (https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.17758). Questions/answers public since 2018, so web contamination is plausible

metadata_hints.metric: F1 (numeracy-aware token F1: F1 = 0 if numbers mismatch) and Exact Match; F1 headline
metadata_hints.n_items_test: 9,622 questions (hidden test; 588 passages). De-facto standard for LLM reports is the public dev set: 9,536 questions (582 passages). Train 77,409 (5,565 passages); total 96,567
metadata_hints.score_at_release_system: Augmented QANet (renamed NAQANet in v2) - authors' QANet with numerical reasoning heads
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Hidden test F1 47.01 / EM 44.07 (dev 49.24 / 46.20). Other baselines (test F1): BERT 32.70, QANet+ELMo 29.67, QANet 28.36, BiDAF 27.49
metadata_hints.lineage: No direct parent; companion AllenNLP reading-comprehension sets (Quoref, ROPES, 2019); DROP contrast sets in Gardner et al. 2020 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.02709)
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: Official-style scoring is brittle for generative LLMs: Hugging Face found float answers never matched due to stop-token/normalization issues and removed DROP from the Open LLM Leaderboard (2023-12-01, https://huggingface.co/blog/open-llm-leaderboard-drop). Wikipedia passages are common in pretraining data

metadata_hints.metric: GLUE score = macro-average over 9 tasks of task metrics (Matthews corr for CoLA; acc/F1 avg for MRPC & QQP; Pearson/Spearman avg for STS-B; accuracy elsewhere, MNLI matched/mismatched)
metadata_hints.n_items_test: ~431k test examples across 9 tasks (v1 Table 1: CoLA 1.1k, SST-2 1.8k, MRPC 1.7k, STS-B 1.4k, QQP 391k, MNLI 20k, QNLI 11k, RTE 3k, WNLI 146) + diagnostic set of 550 sentence pairs (1,100 entailment examples)
metadata_hints.score_at_release_setting: Test set via evaluation server; v1 Table 5 'Avg' column. Caveat: v1 'Avg' values are lower than the simple mean of the per-task scores printed in the same rows (this row's 9 task scores average 67.0), cause not stated. Revised baselines in later arXiv versions/ICLR 2019: best = multi-task BiLSTM+Attn+ELMo 70.0, which the creators later cite as the GLUE score 'at launch' (Nangia & Bowman 2019)
metadata_hints.lineage: Parents: the 9 constituent datasets (2005-2018) and SentEval-style evaluation; successor: SuperGLUE (2019-05); many language-specific clones (e.g., CLUE, Russian SuperGLUE)
metadata_hints.known_contamination_or_defects: WNLI dev set is adversarial due to a data quirk (shared hypotheses between train and dev; v3 paper); NLI components have annotation artifacts (hypothesis-only cues, Gururangan et al. 2018, https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.02324)
